scorecard.note: Add credible sources for the statistics and simplify the visual concepts so they are clearly understandable on a phone screen.

storyboard.ears: Doctors are now finding plastic inside organs that should never see it.
Plastic in human brain tissue jumped by about half in eight years. Whatever we're breathing and eating, it's getting in, and fast.
storyboard.eyes: substance: plastic flecks; cause: Data pours buckets of plastic flecks into the jar and the plastic fills the brain higher with every pour
storyboard.evidence: Nature Medicine (Nihart et al., Univ. of New Mexico) | Nanoplastic concentration in human brain tissue (micrograms per gram) | https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-024-03453-1 | 2026-08-15

storyboard.ears: Plastic showed up in every placenta tested, and in most donors' blood. It isn't staying outside us.
storyboard.eyes: substance: blood with white plastic specks; cause: Data pours each blood sample into the funnel; the blood drains into the flask and the white plastic specks stay caught on the filter
storyboard.evidence: University of New Mexico (placenta, 2024); Environment International (Leslie et al., blood, 2022); New England Journal of Medicine (Marfella et al., artery plaque, 2024) | Share of tested samples/people with microplastics found (percent) | https://www.nejm.org/doi/10.1056/NEJMoa2309822 | 2026-08-15

storyboard.ears: Plastic in artery plaque went with over four times the risk of heart attack, stroke or death. A link, not proven cause.
storyboard.evidence: New England Journal of Medicine (Marfella et al.) | Risk of heart attack, stroke or death: with vs without microplastics in artery plaque | https://www.nejm.org/doi/10.1056/NEJMoa2309822 | 2026-08-15

storyboard.ears: Plastic you can't see is inside us now, and it may be hurting our hearts.
